observations: Three photos show a large office machine wrapped in clear plastic, likely a photocopier or laser printer.
The machine has a beige or off-white casing with visible branding and model text.
The machine is stacked on top of other similar units, suggesting bulk or resale.
The plastic wrap is crinkled and shows signs of handling or storage.
No power cord, paper tray, or control panel is visible in any photo.
The machine appears to be in a warehouse or storage area, with wooden pallets visible in the background.

claims.claim: The AR-M207 is packed with an extensive range of superb performance functions
claims.evidence: No photo shows the machine's control panel, paper tray, or any operational features. The claim cannot be verified from the photos alone.

claims.claim: Low page count, under 20,000 copies. New drum and toner just fitted, no paper jam.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The machine may be non-functional or have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powering on, printing a test page, and operating the control panel.

risks.risk: The machine may be missing critical components such as the power cord, paper tray, or toner cartridge.
risks.proof: Photos of the machine without plastic wrap, showing all sides, control panel, and accessories.

risks.risk: The machine may have been used in a high-dust or industrial environment, affecting print quality or internal wear.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the internal components, especially the drum and fuser, and a video of the machine operating.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with unknown wear

Photos of the machine without plastic wrap, showing all sides, control panel, and accessories.
A video showing the machine powering on and printing a test page.
Close-up photos of the internal components, especially the drum and fuser.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
